### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.snippets

### Question

I'm using `blink.cmp` with `mini.snippet`. The issue occurs when I use `;` to trigger snippet completion. If I type `(;fu)`, after expansion, the output is:  

```lua
(function()

end
```

The closing `)` gets deleted. However, without `;`, the `)` remains intact.  

I suspect the issue comes from `blink.cmp`'s snippet handling, specifically in [`mini_snippet.lua`](https://github.com/Saghen/blink.cmp/blob/main/lua/blink/cmp/sources/snippets/mini_snippets.lua),  Below is my configuration:  
<details><summary>
My Code  
</summary>

```lua
  transform_items = function(_, items)
                local col = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[2]
                local before_cursor = vim.api.nvim_get_current_line():sub(1, col)
                local pos = before_cursor:find(";[%w*]*$")
                -- if not pos then return items end
                if not pos then
                    return vim.tbl_filter(function(item)
                        return item.kind ~= require('blink.cmp.types').CompletionItemKind.Snippet
                    end, items)
                end
                for _, item in ipairs(items) do
                    item.textEdit = {
                        newText = item.insertText or item.label,
                        range = {
                            start = {
                                line = vim.fn.line(".") - 1,
                                character = pos - 1,

                            },
                            ["end"] = {
                                line = vim.fn.line(".") - 1,
                                character = col,
                            },
                        },
                    }

                end

                return vim.tbl_filter(function(item)
                    local kind_snippet = require('blink.cmp.types').CompletionItemKind.Snippet
                    return pos and item.kind == kind_snippet
                end, items)
            end,
```
</details>

I'm unsure how to fix this for a PR to [`mini_snippet.lua`](link_mini_snippet.lua). Any guidance on why the `)` is being deleted and how to properly handle snippet expansion with `;` would be helpful.

comment_data.body:
My first thought is that that is a result of how 'Saghen/blink.cmp' (and 'hrsh7th/nvim-cmp', for that matter) handle combination of `additionalTextEdits` / `textEdit` and snippet expansion. The root cause for this seems to be that 'mini.snippets' always operates in Insert mode which can cause some issues with asynchronous execution (i.e. which text is current at the time of some steps executed). See more information at abeldekat/cmp-mini-snippets#9 and Saghen/blink.cmp#1035.

The second thought is that this might be a consequence of the custom `transform_items` conflicting with [this part](https://github.com/Saghen/blink.cmp/blob/bf810ebe1251dfa756c7fa328e56b0c2e157d313/lua/blink/cmp/sources/snippets/mini_snippets.lua#L125-L134) of the 'blink.cmp'.

As this is seems to be more of a *not* 'mini.snippets' question, I am going to close this. If there will be concrete question about how 'mini.snippets' operates, feel free to ask here.

---

I hope to soon update 'mini.snippets' with a way to suggest its entries via an in-process LSP server. Then it can be used with a regular LSP server handling. Not sure if that would help with this custom "; to trigger snippets" approach.

reply_data.body:
Finally, I found the solution! The missing part was adding:

```lua
vim.schedule(function()
    require("blink.cmp").reload()
end)
```  

It turns out that calling `reload()` ensures the snippet resets properly, and now it works as expected.  

Thank you so much, @echasnovski  Your explanation helped me understand the different edge cases in `blink.cmp` and `nvim-cmp`.  

<details><summary>My Code:</summary>

```lua
   transform_items = function(_, items)
                local col = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[2]
                local before_cursor = vim.api.nvim_get_current_line():sub(1, col)
                local pos = before_cursor:find(";[%w*]*$")
                local reload = function()
                    vim.schedule(function()
                        require("blink.cmp").reload()
                    end)
                end
                -- if not pos then return items end
                if not pos then
                    return vim.tbl_filter(function(item)
                        reload()
                        return item.kind
                            ~= require("blink.cmp.types").CompletionItemKind.Snippet
                    end, items)
                end
                for _, item in ipairs(items) do
                    item.textEdit = {
                        newText = item.insertText or item.label,
                        range = {
                            start = {
                                line = vim.fn.line(".") - 1,
                                character = pos - 1,
                            },
                            ["end"] = {
                                line = vim.fn.line(".") - 1,
                                character = col,
                            },
                        },
                    }
                end
                return vim.tbl_filter(function(item)
                    reload()
                    local kind_snippet = require("blink.cmp.types").CompletionItemKind.Snippet
                    return pos and item.kind == kind_snippet
                end, items)
            end,
```
</details>
 
My apologies for opening a discussion that wasn’t directly related to  `mini.snippet`.

> Thank you so much, @echasnovski Your explanation helped me understand the different edge cases in `blink.cmp` and `nvim-cmp`.

I can't have any credit here. All goes to @abeldekat for dealing with these issues.

> My apologies for opening a discussion that wasn’t directly related to `mini.snippet`.

No worries. You didn't know about that and it wasn't exactly obvious.

---

One small improvement for `local reload = ...` part is to use `vim.schedule_wrap`:

```lua
                local reload = vim.schedule_wrap(require("blink.cmp").reload)
```

Or just use `vim.schedule(require("blink.cmp").reload)` directly both times. Depends on style preferences.
